title: A Chinese City Survived 800 Years — With No Walls | China Travel Expert
description:
Almost every old Chinese city was ringed in a defensive stone wall. This UNESCO-listed town in Yunnan, over 800 years old, never built one — on purpose.

Lijiang Old Town sits at about 2,400m in Yunnan and was inscribed on the UNESCO World Heritage List in 1997. For 470 years, from 1253 to 1723, it was ruled by the Naxi Mu-family chieftains, whose confidence — and welcome to traders on the Tea-Horse Road — meant the town stayed open, with no city wall. (A local tale plays on the chieftains' surname 木, "wood": box it in with a wall-frame and the character becomes 困, "trapped.") What holds the town together instead is water: snowmelt from Jade Dragon Snow Mountain runs through every lane in stone channels, feeding a clever "one well, three pools" system — the top pool for drinking, the middle for washing food, the bottom for laundry. More than 300 old bridges cross the streams, and the Naxi people still use Dongba, one of the last living pictographic scripts on earth.

🧭 Expert Tip: Walk the lanes before 8am. The canals and cobblestones are silent and empty before the tour groups and their flags arrive — it's a completely different town.
